title: Learning Takes Drafts: 13 Years of DSJ (Blog Birthday)
author: Dave Stuart Jr.
summary: Marking his blog's 13th birthday, Dave Stuart Jr. reflects on thirteen years of writing (1,071 articles), video creation, course-building, speaking, and two books, framing all of it through a single governing idea: growth toward mastery — for teachers, writers, parents, and students alike — takes repeated drafts, not a single polished attempt. He illustrates the principle with a story about a graduating senior who wrote, cast, directed, shot, and edited a 56-minute film that was "far from perfect AND completely glorious," reading the student's willingness to put imperfect work into the world as evidence of having apprenticed himself to the same drafting process Stuart describes in his own writing career. Stuart connects his personal growth as a thinker directly to the discipline of writing and publishing regularly, noting that at 28 he didn't know what he didn't know and at 41 the same is surely still true, just about different things. The post closes by pointing readers to an AMA livestream held for the blog's birthday and a short list of Stuart's own favorite past articles, alongside a note of thanks to longtime and brand-new readers alike.
points: Stuart frames his entire 13-year writing career — 1,071 articles, videos, courses, two books — as evidence for a single principle: growth toward mastery takes repeated drafts, never a single finished attempt.
The featured story of a senior's imperfect-but-glorious 56-minute self-made film is used to model what "apprenticing yourself to drafts" looks like for a student rather than just for Stuart himself.
He explicitly ties his own clarity of thought as an educator to the discipline of writing and publishing regularly over thirteen years, not to any innate insight.
He candidly notes that at 41 he still doesn't know what he doesn't know, just as he didn't at 28 — treating ongoing not-knowing as a permanent condition rather than a problem to solve.
The post doubles as a curated "greatest hits" list and an invitation to an AMA livestream, giving new readers an entry point into thirteen years of archives.
quotes: Since then, I've written 1,071 blog articles, created 100s of videos, produced half a dozen courses, spoken all around the country and the world, and published two major books that articulate my philosophy of teaching and its attendant strategies.

Certainly, though, my thinking about teaching and learning and life have become radically clearer than they would have been had I not adopted the practice of writing and creating. Because learning takes drafts.

Growth toward mastery — which is the unique means through which schools promote the long-term flourishing of young people and which is also a key component of a flourishing life — takes drafts and drafts and drafts of learning.

It was both far from perfect AND completely glorious. Here was a young man who was tapping into one of the great superpowers human beings possess: we get better through doing, practicing, putting our work out there, reflecting, and on and on.
It was one of the bravest and most impressive things I've seen a young person do in some time. He has apprenticed himself to the work of learning through drafts.
